title: Burst heuristic drift causing late-occurring 429s during tenant warmups
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a gradual tenant warmup on a Dedicated cluster, multiple customers observed a spike in opaque 429s ~10–20 minutes after the initial traffic ramp instead of during the immediate surge. The behavior affected Hosted and Private tenants using legacy burst heuristics and caused degraded request success rates and user-visible latency spikes for several mid-market customers.

What happened:
- The burst admission heuristic that combines token-bucket state from the proxy and orchestrator drifted under certain lease handoff timings.
- When a warmup created many short-lived concurrent connections, our heuristic incorrectly classified ephemeral traffic as 'sustained' and clipped available burst credits on the orchestrator side.
- Because the proxy continued to accept requests for the configured burst window, the orchestrator started returning 429s after its local token ledger reached zero, ~10–20m post-warmup. This led to customer-visible failures and cascading retries.

Immediate mitigation (done):
- Rolled an emergency orchestration config that extends the grace window for token reconciliation (rollout started 2025-02-14 11:34 UTC, completed to affected Dedicated nodes by 12:05 UTC).
- Rate-limited new tenant warmups at the proxy with an added soft-cap to prevent fast fan-in while reconciliation finishes.
- Contacted impacted customers with status and suggested client-side retry backoffs (CSAT follow-up scheduled).

Root cause analysis (hypothesis validated by traced logs & ledger snapshots):
- Lease handoff race: orchestrator ledger snapshot applied an epoch with truncated transient credits during a leader election, causing net-negative available burst tokens for several tenants.
- Heuristic mismatch: proxy's burst window uses last-request timestamps, but orchestrator uses commit-epoched credit application. The mismatch is benign for steady traffic but becomes visible during warmups and leader churn.
- Missing invariants: there was no fast cross-check for negative reconciliation deltas; we relied on eventual reconciliation which is too slow for short-lived warmups.

Telemetry & evidence:
- Dashboard: /dashboards/quota/tenant-throttles spike at 2025-02-14T11:25Z with correlated orchestrator commit-latency increase.
- Traces: sample trace IDs: trace-0a9f3345, trace-0b7d11c2 showing proxy accepted then got 429 from orchestrator 12m later.
- Logs: orchestrator logs show ledger-apply errors and epoch rollbacks: ORCH-ERR-11235.

Planned permanent fixes:
1) Reconcile algorithm change (runtime): switch to conservative optimistic-credit propagation during warmups by pre-allocating a small safety buffer on orchestrator and proxy. (owner: Diego)
2) Stronger invariants: add an invariant check that raises reconciliation alerts when orchestrator's delta < -threshold and auto-triggers conservative throttling to avoid opaque 429s. (owner: Priya Rao)
3) Leader handoff hardening: ensure ledger snapshots applied are idempotent and include tombstone markers to avoid truncated credit states after failover. (owner: Infra)
4) Test harness: add a simulated warmup fuzz test in integration suite that runs leader election during high-concurrency startup to catch this class of regressions. (owner: QA)

Code & artifacts:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4578 (cherry-picked runtime-1.19.1)
- Followup RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QS/Burst+Reconciliation+Rethink
- Runbook update: /runbooks/quota/burst-healing.md (patched 2025-02-15)

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Diego: ship conservative-propagation patch & deploy to canary (ETA 2025-02-18) — IN PROGRESS
- Priya: implement reconciliation alert and auto-throttle (ETA 2025-02-25) — TODO
- Infra: add persistent ledger tombstones to snapshot flow and test (ETA 2025-03-03) — TODO
- QA: add warmup+election fuzz test and include in pre-release checks (ETA 2025-02-28) — TODO
- PM: prepare customer RCA and postmortem for affected tenants (ETA 2025-02-21) — TODO

Acceptance criteria for closing ticket:
- Canary deployment shows no post-warmup opaque 429s during simulated leader election tests for 48 hours.
- Reconciliation alert triggers on synthetic negative deltas and auto-throttles correctly.
- Customer follow-up and compensation plan complete and approved by Support & Sales.
